transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I... um, I guess I'm here because I just... I can't stop feeling like I'm a danger to people. I had this... this near-miss at work recently, and it just... it feels like proof that I'm a disappointment. Like I'm not meant to be a nurse at all. Sometimes I just think everyone would be better off without me getting in the way.
Have you been having thoughts of hurting yourself?

I... no. I don't have a plan to actually do anything. I just... I don't know. Sometimes I just think it would be easier if I didn't wake up. Or if I could just... disappear. That way I wouldn't mess anything else up.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Um... a while, I guess. Maybe... a year and two months? It kind of started after I graduated high school... right around when I began my college classes and started working full-time at the clinic.
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Um... no. Not really. 

I used to do things to clear my head after class... like jogging, or knitting. Sometimes cooking or reading. But now... I don't know. I just get home and sit on my bed in my scrubs. I just can't really make myself care about any of it anymore.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Um... like I just said... no. Not really. 

None of the stuff I used to do... the jogging or reading or whatever... none of it really matters right now. Like I mentioned, I just sit on my bed when I get home. I just don't care about any of it anymore.
Are there any small things that happen during the day that still bring you a little bit of happiness?

Not really... no. 

I mean, I don't know what else to say. Like I told you, I used to like jogging or knitting, or reading... but I just don't have it in me anymore. I just sit there in my scrubs. Nothing really feels good right now.
Can you think of any time recently when you felt even slightly happy or satisfied?

I... I really don't think so. I mean... I feel like I'm repeating myself, but... no. 

I just... I go to class, I come home, I sit on my bed. That's it. I don't... I don't feel anything from the cooking or the knitting or... any of it anymore. It's just... blank.
Have you experienced a significant increase or decrease in your appetite?

I guess... a decrease. I don't really think about food much lately. 

Usually I just... forget to eat until it's pretty late. Then I'll just, I don't know, force down some crackers or have some coffee. I haven't really been trying to lose weight or anything, but... I did notice my work pants are getting kind of loose. So... yeah. Less appetite.
Has this feeling of being a disappointment and not finding pleasure in activities been constant over the past year and two months, or have you had periods where you felt better?

I guess it's been pretty constant. Um... yeah, about a year and two months. I haven't really had any periods where I felt better. 

It just... it started right after I graduated high school. When I began my college classes and... the full-time clinic work. It's just been like this ever since.
Have you experienced any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt even slight enjoyment or interest in social interactions over the past year and two months?
Um... no. Not really. I just... I don't really talk to anyone unless I have to for work or class. I haven't really wanted to. So... no.
Has your feeling of being a disappointment gotten worse over the past year and two months?

Um... yeah. I think it's gotten worse. That's... kind of why I finally came in. 

I just... I can't stop feeling like I'm a disappointment. And... a danger, honestly. There was this... a near-miss at work. And it just... I don't know, it feels like it proves I'm not meant to be a nurse. Like... maybe everyone would just be better off without me.
Have you had any periods where your feelings of being a disappointment and not enjoying activities went away, even if just for a little while?

Um... no. Like I... I think I said earlier, it hasn't really gone away at all. It's just been the whole year and two months. Ever since I graduated high school and... started my college classes and working full-time at the clinic. It's just been constant.
Have you had more than one episode of feeling this way, or has it been one continuous period?

Um... yeah, like I said, it's just been continuous. Just... one long period. For the whole year and two months since I graduated high school and started my classes and the clinic job. It hasn't stopped.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you didn't feel like a disappointment and were able to enjoy activities?
No... I don't think so. I haven't had a break from it.
Have you ever felt this way before the year and two months you mentioned?
Um... no. Not really. Just... just since then, I guess.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over the past year and two months?

Um... yeah, I guess. It's... it's not great. I just lie there at night, mostly. Just... replaying charts in my head, or going over medication calculations. And um... when I do finally fall asleep, I usually wake up before my alarm even goes off. I just wake up already exhausted and... kind of scared that I missed something.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt completely back to normal and didn't have these feelings of being a disappointment?
No. I don't... I don't think I've had two weeks like that. It's just been the same.
Have you usually felt this way for most of the day, every day, over the past year and two months?
Um... yeah, I guess so. Most days. Just... all day.
Have you had any periods of significant improvement in your mood that lasted for at least two months over the past year and two months?
No. I haven't... I haven't really felt better. Not for that long.
Have you ever felt this way before in your life, before the year and two months you mentioned?
Um... I don't think so. I don't really remember feeling quite like this before.
